To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) voltage-activated Ca sparks in frog skeletal muscle fibers are produced by the opening of one or two RyR Ca2 + release channels; and (b) tetracaine inhibits the opening of one but not both of the channels that are active in the absence of inhibitor.

(a) a single RyR channel is unlikely to be the Ca2+ source for voltage-activated Ca sparks in intact frog muscle fibers, but (b) the properties of Ca2 + sparks in tetraca ine are those expected if two or more active Ca2+ release sites are involved in the generation of normal voltage-activated Ca spark events.

voltage-activated Ca sparks in intact frog skeletal muscle fibers have properties that are well described by our computational model and that the single-channel current of the RyR Ca channel is ≤1 pA under physiological ion conditions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the properties and regulation of voltage-activated Ca sparks in skeletal muscle fibers.
the mechanisms that underlie Ca2+ sparks, which are elementary Ca2+ release events in muscle and other excitable tissues.
understanding the mechanisms by which Ca2+ sparks occur and propagate in intact frog muscle fibers.

the results support the conclusion of two or more RyR Ca2+-release channels per spark in frog skeletal muscle fibers.

the number of active channels per voltage-activated Ca spark in frog skeletal muscle is 1–5, but is usually 1–3, and that tetracaine is a useful tool for distinguishing between one and greater-than-one active RyR channel per spark.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the voltage-activated sparks in intact frog skeletal muscle fibers are produced by the coordinated activation of one to five RyR Ca2+-release channels.

the properties of voltage-activated sparks in intact frog skeletal muscle fibers are well described by our computational model with a single active RyR channel per spark, provided that (a) a small fraction (≤10%) of the sparks are produced by two active RyR channels per spark, or (b) the RyR channel has a single-channel Ca2+-current amplitude of <1 pA.

the properties of Ca2 sparks in frog intact muscle fibers are consistent with the opening of 1–5 active RyR Ca channels, and that the number of active channels per spark may vary from fiber to fiber and from spark to spark.
The main takeaway from our work is that
voltage-activated Ca sparks are produced by more than one active RyR Ca channel.
the single-channel Ca current of the RyR is 0.6-1.2 picoamperes.
